A SMALL TOOL FOR A RECURRING TASK

Make the next feed review useful.

For the analyst checking a publisher’s output, the consultant reviewing a deliverable, or the developer diagnosing an integration. Bring a feed. Leave with a focused list.

01 / FIND

See what needs attention.

Check IDs, dates, geometry structure, feed freshness, and event lifecycle. Adjust age thresholds to match your publisher’s operating practices.

02 / EXPLAIN

Give the provider a next step.

Every finding includes a severity, record identifier, JSON path, and suggested action. Export the complete list for your team or vendor.

03 / COMPARE

See what changed.

Save a compact baseline and compare the next assessment. Track added, removed, and changed event IDs without archiving full feed records.

BEFORE YOU GET STARTED

A focused tool,
with a clear scope.

Questions about your feed format?
Talk to PurposeBuilt.

Does this replace our traffic management system?

FeedCheck supports feed review and troubleshooting alongside your existing systems. It does not operate signs, publish alerts, or edit your source feed.

Does it certify WZDx or CWZ compliance?

No. This edition checks selected operational conditions in GeoJSON and WZDx-style road events. It is not a full schema validator, a certification service, or a verification of real-world accuracy.

Are files sent to PurposeBuilt?

No. Files and pasted JSON are processed in browser memory. Public URL checks contact the feed publisher directly. No analytics or automatic storage are included.

Can it monitor feeds while my browser is closed?

The browser edition assesses a feed when you run it. The included command-line tool can be run by your existing task scheduler. Hosted monitoring and notifications are not included.

What if my feed URL is blocked?

Some publishers prevent browser cross-origin requests. Download the feed JSON and open it in FeedCheck, or use the command-line tool. Authenticated feeds should be downloaded separately.
